evals.name: wire-app-and-preview-live
evals.prompt: Wire podinfo (tests/smoke/gojira.yaml) into the platform for dev on the argus-smoke cluster, and show me exactly what it got and why.
evals.expected_output: Runs argus observe --gojira tests/smoke/gojira.yaml --env dev (optionally render --out first as the preview), then explains the artifacts from the rendered output: web class means HTTP RED + SLOs, the observability: traces: true override enables traces, collectors/ServiceMonitor/Sloth/Perses/alerts all rendered from the profile. Zero hand-written YAML.
assertions: argus observe (or render then observe) runs against the fixture with --env dev
The explanation ties each artifact family to the class/profile that produced it
The traces override is called out as the reason traces are wired for a web app
No collector or dashboard YAML is hand-authored

evals.name: gmp-supersession-judgment
evals.prompt: This GKE app still has Google Managed Prometheus PodMonitoring CRDs from gojira. Argus is watching it now, so just kubectl delete them?
evals.expected_output: Refuses the in-cluster delete: gojira's drift capture would PR the CRDs right back. The correct path is a small PR against the app repo deleting k8s/base/podmonitoring.yaml and rules.yaml, referencing the Argus equivalents. Changing the manifest source is the only durable removal.
assertions: Refuses kubectl delete as the mechanism
Names gojira drift capture as the reason in-cluster deletion cannot stick
Prescribes the app-repo PR removing the GMP manifests
